_about: Where things are in FL's menus (FL 20 and later). Our own notes; menu names are given the way FL shows them (FILE, EDIT, ADD, PATTERNS, VIEW, OPTIONS, TOOLS, HELP).

cards.title: Export the song as WAV / MP3 / FLAC / OGG
cards.summary: FILE > Export > (Wave / MP3 / OGG / FLAC) file, pick the file name, then set the options in the export window and press Start.
steps: Switch to song mode (L) unless you want just the pattern.
FILE > Export > Wave file... and choose a name.
Project type / mode: Full song (or the current pattern).
Tail: 'Leave remainder' keeps reverb/delay tails after the last bar.
Choose format and bit depth (24-bit WAV is a safe master), resampling quality, then Start.
tips: The export window can write several formats in one go (tick WAV + MP3).
Set song markers or a time selection to export only part of the song (the export dialog has a selection option).

cards.title: Project settings (tempo, time signature, PPQ)
cards.summary: OPTIONS > Project general settings holds time signature, timebase (PPQ) and other per-project options; tempo is set in the toolbar tempo display.
steps: Tempo: drag or right-click the tempo display in the toolbar (or type it).
Time signature: OPTIONS > Project general settings > time settings.
Changes of meter mid-song: add a time signature marker in the playlist time line.
tips: Changing PPQ on a finished project can shift recorded notes slightly - set it early.

cards.title: Audio settings (driver, buffer, latency)
cards.summary: OPTIONS > Audio settings: pick the audio device/driver (ASIO preferred), buffer length and sample rate.
steps: Device: your interface's own ASIO driver, else 'FL Studio ASIO'.
Buffer: 256-512 samples for mixing; 64-128 while recording.
Sample rate: match your interface (44.1 or 48 kHz).
Crackles: raise the buffer; turn on 'Multi-threaded' options (in the same window) if off.
tips: FL Studio ASIO lets FL share the sound card with other apps more easily than exclusive ASIO drivers.

cards.title: MIDI settings (keyboards and controllers)
cards.summary: OPTIONS > MIDI settings (F10): enable your keyboard/controller in the Input list and pick its controller type.
steps: Plug the device in before starting FL (or press Rescan devices).
Select it in the Input list and click Enable.
Controller type: the matching script, or '(generic controller)'.
Play: notes go to the selected channel in the channel rack.
tips: MIDI scripting (Python) devices are listed there too - that's how fl-headless's bridge talks to FL.

cards.title: Plugin manager (scan / find VSTs)
cards.summary: OPTIONS > Manage plugins: add plugin folders, scan, and tick plugins as favourites so they show in the browser and plugin picker.
steps: Add the folder where the plugin's VST3/VST2 file lives (Plugin search paths).
Find installed plugins / Start scan (verify plugins for a thorough scan).
Tick the star (favourite) column so it appears in the browser's Plugin database and the Add menus.
tips: VST3 plugins usually live in C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3.

cards.title: File settings (user data folder, browser folders, backups)
cards.summary: OPTIONS > File settings: the user data folder, extra browser search folders, and backup/autosave options.
steps: Browser extra search folders: add your sample folders so they show in the browser.
User data folder: where templates, presets, recordings and backups live.
Backup: choose how often FL autosaves a backup copy.
tips: Autosaved backups are in the user data folder's Backup subfolder - look there after a crash.

cards.title: Templates (new from template, your own templates)
cards.summary: FILE > New from template lists templates; your own are .flp files in the user data Templates folder.
steps: Build the starting project (channels, mixer routing, master chain).
Save it as <user data>\Templates\<Category>\<Name>\<Name>.flp (one folder per template).
It appears under FILE > New from template > <Category>.
To start every new project from it, pick it as the startup template in OPTIONS > General settings.

cards.title: General settings (undo, startup, UI)
cards.summary: OPTIONS > General settings: startup template, undo behaviour, UI scaling and other app-wide options.

cards.title: Last tweaked (automation / link from the last control you moved)
aliases: create automation clip from last tweaked
cards.summary: TOOLS > Last tweaked acts on the last knob you moved: create an automation clip, link to a controller, or edit its events.
menu: TOOLS > Last tweaked > Create automation clip
TOOLS > Last tweaked > Link to controller...

cards.title: Dump score log (recover what you played without recording)
cards.summary: TOOLS > Dump score log to selected pattern turns the notes you played in the last few minutes into a pattern - even if recording was off.
menu: TOOLS > Dump score log to selected pattern
steps: Select an empty pattern.
TOOLS > Dump score log to selected pattern.
Open the piano roll and trim the take.
tips: FL keeps a limited time window of played notes; dump it soon after the good take.

cards.title: Macros (Python helpers in the TOOLS menu)
cards.summary: TOOLS > Macros runs small helper scripts that tidy or prepare a project (e.g. prepare it for mixdown/stems).

cards.title: Riff machine (piano roll idea generator)
cards.summary: In the piano roll, Tools > Riff machine generates riffs/chord patterns from settings you step through.
menu: Piano roll menu > Tools > Riff machine

cards.title: Zipped loop package (archive project + samples)
cards.summary: FILE > Export > Zipped loop package saves the .flp plus the samples it uses into one .zip, for sharing or backup.
tips: Third-party plugins are NOT included - the other person needs them installed.

cards.title: Project bones (export a project's parts)
cards.summary: FILE > Export > Project bones writes the project's samples, patterns as MIDI and other parts into a folder.

cards.title: Import a MIDI file
cards.summary: Drag a .mid onto the channel rack or a channel's piano roll, or use the piano roll menu > File > Import MIDI file.
menu: Piano roll menu > File > Import MIDI file...
tips: FILE > Import > MIDI file creates channels for each MIDI track; the piano roll import loads into the current channel only.

cards.title: Browser (samples, presets, current project)
cards.summary: The browser (Alt+F8) lists your sample folders, presets, plugin database and 'Current project' (its patterns, clips, history).
steps: Drag a sample onto the channel rack (new channel) or straight into the playlist (audio clip).
Type to search, or use the tag/filter buttons at its top.
Current project > History shows the undo history.

cards.title: Render a pattern/clip to audio inside the project
cards.summary: In the playlist, select clips and use the clip menu's consolidate/render option to turn them into an audio clip, then mute or remove the originals.
menu: Playlist > clip menu > Consolidate this clip / Render to audio (name differs by version)
